# [\#18 Issue](https://github.com/dEhiN/CanadianBusinessCollege--FullStackWebApplicationDiploma/issues/18) `open`: Create controller functions for User endpoints

#### <img src="https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/26848686?u=6c1f8b72ff786312cb5de7ffb1fbb1a9b8f2b464&v=4" width="50">[dEhiN](https://github.com/dEhiN) opened issue at [2026-05-25 09:23](https://github.com/dEhiN/CanadianBusinessCollege--FullStackWebApplicationDiploma/issues/18):

~Create the API app routes logic for interactions with the _Users_ collection.~

Based on recent structural changes, this issue has been updated and now entails creating the controller logic for the Users endpoints.

#### <img src="https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/26848686?u=6c1f8b72ff786312cb5de7ffb1fbb1a9b8f2b464&v=4" width="50">[dEhiN](https://github.com/dEhiN) commented at [2026-05-26 21:33](https://github.com/dEhiN/CanadianBusinessCollege--FullStackWebApplicationDiploma/issues/18#issuecomment-4549150556):

Adding the relevant route information from issue #11:

- [ ] **GET** `/api/users/user-profile`
_Returns_: User profile page for the logged in user. If no user is logged in, an HTTP 401 "Unauthorized" message is returned.

- [ ] **GET** `/api/users/user-trips` - 
_Returns_: Saved user trip history for the logged in user. If no user is logged in, an HTTP 401 "Unauthorized" message is returned.

- [ ] **GET** `/api/users/user-trips/filter` - 
_Data Sent_: Search parameters sent as query parameters to allow for query filtering of the logged in user's trip data. If no user is logged in, an HTTP 401 "Unauthorized" message is returned.
_Data Validated_: No because data is only being retrieved from the database. Will need to handle situation where search parameters don't make sense.
_Data Returned_: Trip data in the form of JSON data.

- [x] **POST** `/api/users/create-account` - Account creation
_Data Sent_: The information needed to create a new account for a user.
_Data Validated_: Yes to ensure the sent data fits the JSON schema for user data. This prepares the data to be saved to the database.
_Data Returned_: A success message with the user id as JSON data.

- [x] **POST** `/api/users/login-account` - Account login
_Data Sent_: The information needed to log into an account, notably a username and password.
_Data Validated_: No because this data is not being saved to the database.
_Data Returned_: A message of success or failure in the form of JSON data. If the login was successful, the correct user id should also be sent.

#### <img src="https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/26848686?u=6c1f8b72ff786312cb5de7ffb1fbb1a9b8f2b464&v=4" width="50">[dEhiN](https://github.com/dEhiN) commented at [2026-05-27 07:49](https://github.com/dEhiN/CanadianBusinessCollege--FullStackWebApplicationDiploma/issues/18#issuecomment-4552548833):

While testing, realized that setting up the User data fields `CreditCardDetails.CardId` and `VehicleDetails.VehicleId` as aliases for the Mongoose models to the auto-generated `_id` field isn't working so well. For example, this is what gets returned due to the alias setup in the Mongoose User schema:

```
VehicleDetails: [
    {
      OwnerName: 'David Watson',
      VehicleMake: 'Honda',
      VehicleModel: 'Civic',
      VehicleColour: 'Midnight Black',
      LicensePlate: 'ABCD123',
      _id: new ObjectId('6a169d14cf34b27b72963ee3'),
      VehicleId: '6a169d14cf34b27b72963ee3',
      id: '6a169d14cf34b27b72963ee3'
    }
]
```

The schema code in `user_models.js` governing this alias is:

```
toJSON: { virtuals: true },
toObject: { virtuals: true },
virtuals: {
    VehicleId: {
        get() {
            return this._id.toHexString();
        },
        set(value) {
            this._id = new mongoose.Types.ObjectId(value);
        }
    }
}
```

After playing around with those three fields by commenting out one or more of them in different combinations, I can only either get the `_id` field to show or all 3 fields to show. That is, either `_id` shows and `id` plus `VehicleId` don't show, or all of them show.

Perhaps it might be better to not rely on the database auto-generated id. If so, it might make sense to modify the JSON structure so that the arrays `VehicleDetails` and `CreditCardDetails` have a field showing the total number of vehicles or cards in the user's account, and then each vehicle/card will have a simple, sequential number. This would potentially make the logic easier to handle since the field showing the total would just need to be read or updated - depending on the CRUD operation - and both the backend and frontend can more easily associate each vehicle/card with their unique id.

Will need to think about this.

#### <img src="https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/26848686?u=6c1f8b72ff786312cb5de7ffb1fbb1a9b8f2b464&v=4" width="50">[dEhiN](https://github.com/dEhiN) commented at [2026-05-27 07:54](https://github.com/dEhiN/CanadianBusinessCollege--FullStackWebApplicationDiploma/issues/18#issuecomment-4552580780):

Currently the trip JSON Schema contains the following setup:

```
"VehicleDetails": {
    "type": "array",
    "description": "An array of user vehicles. Each one includes details about the vehicle including the vehicle owner.",
    "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "VehicleId": {
                "type": "string",
                "description": "A unique identifier that represents this vehicle in the system/db."
            },
            // Other properties
        }
    }
}
```

Perhaps the Schema could be modified to be something like this:

```
"VehicleDetails": {
    "type": "object",
    "description": "An object containing details about all the vehicles the user owns or has used with the DD service.",
    "properties": {
        "TotalVehicles": {
            "type": "number",
            "description": "A running tally of the total number of unique vehicles the user has used with the service."
        },
        "Vehicles": {
            "type": "array",
            "description": "An array of user vehicles. Each one includes details about the vehicle including the vehicle owner.",
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "VehicleId": {
                        "type": "number",
                        "description": "A sequential number indicating which vehicle this is out of all of the user's vehicles."
                    },
                    // Other properties
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

In other words, the `VehicleDetails` field will become an object with 2 keys. The first will be `TotalVehicles` which will be a number representing all the vehicles the user has used with the service. (This will most likely be only 1 for most users, but it's possible over time, some repeat users of the service might have several vehicles they need driven.) The second will then be the array of objects like before, but it will be called `Vehicles`. In addition, each vehicle object still has a field called `VehicleId` but it's a sequential number added by the server logic. This keeps things simpler in many ways and makes it easier to associate the id of a specific vehicle with the vehicle details.

The same idea could probably be applied to the credit card details as well.

#### <img src="https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/26848686?u=6c1f8b72ff786312cb5de7ffb1fbb1a9b8f2b464&v=4" width="50">[dEhiN](https://github.com/dEhiN) commented at [2026-05-27 08:34](https://github.com/dEhiN/CanadianBusinessCollege--FullStackWebApplicationDiploma/issues/18#issuecomment-4552856029):

For the sake of the class project, the schema specs will be changed to only have one credit card and vehicle. So, no array.

This means the `VehicleDetails` and `CreditCardDetails` become single objects. There are no `_id` fields for them, and there is also no `IsDefault` field for the credit card. For now, a user can only save one card and vehicle to their account.
